Consult Summary:
- 5 days of dry cough and constant rhinorrhea with subjective fevers/chills and myalgias in a patient with diabetes and hypertension; presentation most consistent with an acute viral upper respiratory infection; safety-net and supportive care advised.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Dry cough and continuous runny nose for ~5 days.
- Cough: Dry; frequent (every 20–30 minutes); no sputum; no hemoptysis; no chest pain; no dyspnea; no pleuritic pain.
- Nasal symptoms: Constant rhinorrhea; green discharge; no epistaxis; no reported facial/sinus pain.
- Systemic: Feels hot with chills; no measured temperature; myalgias present; no headache; no visual changes; no rash.
- GI: Brief diarrhea at onset; resolved. No vomiting. Eating and drinking normally.
- GU: Passing urine normally; no increased frequency or thirst. Weight stable.
- Respiratory history: No chronic chest problems; occasional wheeze only with intense exercise. No history of recurrent chest infections.
- Self-care: Using Lemsip (2–3/day) with symptomatic throat relief at bedtime.
- Timeline/progression: Symptoms started ~5 days ago; ongoing; no red-flag progression reported.

Past Medical History:
- Type 2 diabetes mellitus: Patient reports a “normal” diabetes blood test about 3 weeks ago (no values provided). No current hyperglycemia symptoms reported.
- Hypertension: Last BP check “a while ago”; stability unknown.

Medications:
- Metformin (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Lisinopril (patient states “200”; dose/route/frequency not documented; dose unclear).
- Lemsip (contains paracetamol; OTC; as needed).
- Allergies: No known drug allergies. Seasonal hay fever (environmental).

Social History:
- Lives with partner and a dog.
- Occupation: Office manager.
- Alcohol: Occasional (“odd” drink); exact type/amount not clearly documented.
- Smoking: Not recorded.

Family History:
- Not recorded.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: Not recorded (no home temperature; telehealth visit).
- Examination findings: Not recorded.

Investigations:
- None performed during this consult.
- Patient reports a “normal” diabetes blood test ~3 weeks ago (no details provided).

Assessment & Plan:
- Overall Impression:
  - Acute viral upper respiratory infection with cough and rhinorrhea. No features suggesting pneumonia or severe sinusitis at this time. Diabetes increases risk for secondary bacterial infection; close monitoring advised.

- DDx Integration (brief):
  - Acute viral URI/acute viral bronchitis: Supported by 5-day dry cough, rhinorrhea, myalgias/chills; no dyspnea or chest pain. Opposing: green nasal discharge (nonspecific) and diabetes as risk for bacterial complications.
  - Viral influenza-like illness (including COVID-19): Supported by myalgias/chills and acute cough; Opposing: no documented fever, prominent rhinorrhea.
  - Acute bacterial rhinosinusitis: Supported by green discharge; Opposing: duration <10 days, absence of severe features or facial pain.

- Issue 1: Acute cough with rhinorrhea, likely viral URI
  - Plan:
    - Supportive care: Continue Lemsip as needed; avoid taking any additional paracetamol-containing products concurrently.
    - Consider limited use of cough syrup only at night if cough prevents sleep; avoid daytime use to allow effective airway clearance.
    - Obtain a thermometer and monitor temperature.
    - Safety-net: Seek re-evaluation if any of the following occur: persistent or spiking temperature >37.5–38°C, worsening cough, new purulent sputum, hemoptysis, epistaxis, shortness of breath, or chest pain. In such cases, antibiotics may be considered if bacterial infection suspected.
    - Expected course: Viral symptoms often improve over 1–2 weeks; cough may persist longer.

- Issue 2: Type 2 diabetes mellitus
  - Current status: No polydipsia/polyuria; eating/drinking well; no home glucose monitoring equipment.
  - Plan: Continue metformin; maintain regular diabetes check-ups with GP as advised.

- Issue 3: Hypertension
  - Current status: On lisinopril; last BP check “a while ago”; control status unclear.
  - Plan: Continue lisinopril; arrange/attend routine BP monitoring with GP. Medication dose unclear—confirm at next review.

- General plan items:
  - Medication safety: Avoid duplication of paracetamol-containing products.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: No vitals recorded (including temperature, pulse, BP, SpO2); no physical exam; smoking status not documented; medication doses/routes/frequencies not documented; no allergy verification beyond NKDA/environmental.
- Conflicts: None between transcript and DDx regarding diagnosis. Lisinopril “200” reported by patient—dose unclear.
- Transcript quality: Generally clear; some incomplete responses (e.g., smoking status). No objective measurements available due to telehealth setting.
